messages.author: Rachael Jack
messages.title: Open-Rank Faculty Positions in Computational Mind & Behavior | Vanderbilt University
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues

We're hiring at Vanderbilt!  Join us in building Computational Mind & Behavior.

We use computation to make mind and behavior explainable—and mind and behavior to make new forms of computation possible.

At Vanderbilt University's College of Connected Computing, we're building Computational Mind & Behavior (CMB) around this two-way scientific ambition. We're recruiting exceptional scholars at Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor levels to help shape our scientific directions, collaborations, and intellectual community.

Our vision is to discover the principles that generate intelligence and behavior—from brains and individuals to interacting agents, groups, cultures, and societies—and understand what happens as human and artificial intelligence become increasingly intertwined.

We're particularly interested in four interconnected research directions:
🧠 Brain & Cognition / NeuroAI — How biological and artificial systems perceive, learn, reason, decide, and adapt.
💬 Language, Embodiment & Interaction — How minds communicate and connect through language, multimodal signals, embodied behavior, and human–AI interaction.
🤝 Strategic Social Behavior — How cooperation, competition, social inference, and strategic decision-making emerge among interacting agents.
🌐 Networks & Collective Intelligence — How behavior and intelligence emerge across social networks, cultures, populations, and human–AI collectives.

We welcome outstanding researchers from computing, AI, psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience, and related disciplines. We value deep disciplinary expertise, ambitious scientific questions, innovative computational approaches, and the potential to forge new connections across fields.

Join us in building an intellectual community that connects fundamental discoveries about intelligence and behavior with new computational ideas, methods, and technologies.

Interested in joining us?
We'd be delighted to hear from prospective candidates and discuss our scientific vision, recruitment priorities, and opportunities within CMB.

Contact
Prof. Rachael E. Jack
Area Head, Computational Mind & Behavior
EMAIL_REDACTED

How to apply
Application links:
Assistant Professor: https://lnkd.in/eWVhNVtY
Associate & Full Professor: https://lnkd.in/edtYbiym

In Interfolio, select “Humans, Computing and Society” as your primary review area; identify a secondary review area, if applicable (e.g., Physical Intelligence). In your cover letter, explicitly state your interest in Computational Mind & Behavior (CMB).

Explore our scientific vision: https://lnkd.in/eW3YVmev

Full consideration deadline: December 1, 2026.

Please share widely with colleagues and potential candidates!


Prof. Rachael E. Jack, Ph.D.
Professor of Computational Social Cognition
Professor of Psychology
Area Lead: Computational Mind & Behavior
Co-Director: MOSAIC
Past-President | Society for Affective Science
Editor-in-Chief | Advances in Psychological Science Open
College of Connected Computing
Vanderbilt University
Nashville, Tennessee, USA

messages.title: Many Funded Ph.D. Positions at the International Max Planck Research School for Intelligent Systems (IMPRS-IS)
messages.body_html:
The Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and the Universities of Stuttgart and Tübingen collaborate to offer an interdisciplinary doctoral program, the International Max Planck Research School for Intelligent Systems (IMPRS-IS). This doctoral program will accept its 11th generation of doctoral researchers in 2027.

This school is a key element of Baden-Württemberg’s Cyber Valley initiative to accelerate basic research and commercial development in artificial intelligence and robotics. We seek students who want to earn a doctorate while contributing to world-leading research in areas such as:

•  Artificial Intelligence
•  Biomedical Technology
•  Computational Cognitive Science
•  Computer Vision and Graphics
•  Control Systems and Optimization
•  Data Science
•  Haptics and Human-Computer Interaction
•  Machine Learning
•  Micro- and Nano-Robotics
•  Natural Language Processing
•  Neuroscience
•  Perceptual Inference
•  Robotics and Human-Robot Interaction
•  Soft Robotics and Materials

Our renowned faculty include Sahar Abdelnabi, Rediet Abebe, Amirreza Aghakhani, Aamir Ahmad, Buse Aktaş, Frank Allgöwer, Maksym Andriushchenko, Kai Arras, Julian Berberich, Philipp Berens, Matthias Bethge, Wieland Brendel, Andrés Bruhn, Andreas Bulling, Martin Butz, Manfred Claassen, Alberto Comoretto, Maximilian Dax, Stephan Eckstein, Benedikt Ehinger, Carsten Eickhoff, Veronika Eyring, Peter Gehler, Andreas Geiger, Jonas Geiping, Antonia Georgopoulou, Martin A. Giese, Moritz Hardt, Florian Hartmann, Daniel Häufle, Matthias Hein, Philipp Hennig, Niels Henze, Katharina V. Hoebel, Christian Holm, Andrea Iannelli, Christoph Keplinger, Miriam Klopotek, Jens Kober, Mario Krenn, Katherine Kuchenbecker, Hilde Kuehne, Anja Lauer, Hendrik Lensch, Anna Levina, Shiwei Liu, Sabine Ludwigs, Jakob Macke, Georg Martius, Kristof Meding, Shohei Mori, Michael Muehlebach, Philipp Müller, Sven Nahnsen, Mathias Niepert, Antonio Orvieto, Aniket Pal, Nico Pfeifer, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael Pradel, C. David Remy, Kerstin Ritter, Philipp Rothemund, Konstantin Rusch, Renate Sachse, Samira Samadi, Harry Scells, Dieter Schmalstieg, Syn Schmitt, Bernhard Schölkopf, Sabine Schulte im Walde, Janneke Schwaner, Michael Sedlmair, Chelsea Sidrane, Thomas Speck, Steffen Staab, Ingo Steinwart, Alexander Verl, Ulrike von Luxburg, Daniel Weiskopf, Felix Wichmann, Bob Williamson, Maria Wirzberger, Andreas Wortmann, and Thomas Wortmann. 

Associated faculty include Franz Baumdicker, Marcel Binz, Sebastian Damrich, Peter Dayan, Kerol Djoumessi, Jonathan Fiene, Michèle Finck, Volker Franz, Ksenia Keplinger, Jan Knippers, Achim Menges, Trang-Anh E. Nghiem, Kay Nieselt, Senya Polikovsky, Peter Pott, Gunther Richter, Cornelia Sindermann, and Isabell Wochner. 

Intelligent systems that can successfully perceive, act, and learn in complex environments hold great potential for aiding society. We seek doctoral students who are curious, creative, and passionate about research to join our school and help advance human knowledge about intelligent systems.

• Admitted students can join our program starting in spring of 2027.
• You will be mentored by our internationally renowned faculty.
• You will register as a university doctoral student and conduct research.
• IMPRS-IS offers a wide variety of scientific seminars, workshops, and social activities.
• All aspects of our program are in English.
• Your doctoral degree will be conferred when you successfully complete your doctoral project.
• Our dedicated staff members will assist you throughout your time as a doctoral student.

People with a strong academic background and a master’s degree (conferred or expected soon) in Engineering, Computer Science, Cognitive Science, Mathematics, Control Theory, Neuroscience, Materials Science, Physics, or related fields should apply.

IMPRS-IS is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to excellence through diversity and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, sex, disability, sexual orientation, national origin, religion, marital status, gender identity, or any other non-job-related criteria. We believe in the importance of a multicultural community of students, faculty, and staff who seek to advance our commitment to diversity and inclusion. IMPRS-IS strives to create and maintain working and learning environments that are inclusive, equitable, and welcoming.

Admission will be competitive. If selected, you will receive funding via an employment contract, subject to the rules of the Max Planck Society and the two participating universities.  

You can apply at https://imprs.is.mpg.de/application before November 15, 2026 (End of Day, AoE). Finalists will be invited to selection interviews that will take place from February 18 to 26, 2027.

For further information, please visit https://imprs.is.mpg.de

topics.title: Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence (SUSHI) Symposium 2027
topics.snippet: Dear Colleagues, We wish to invite you to attend the SUSHI (Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence

messages.author: Daniel Bush
messages.title: Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence (SUSHI) Symposium 2027
messages.body_html:
Dear Colleagues,

We wish to invite you to attend the SUSHI (Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence) symposium, a two-day satellite event taking place in Glasgow immediately before the 7th International Conference on Memory (ICOM-7) next year.

SUSHI will bring together leading laboratories using human intracranial single-neuron recordings to investigate learning, memory, and higher-order cognition. The symposium is intended as a focused forum for discussing recent advances, emerging methods, and future directions in the study of human single-neuron activity.

The programme will consist exclusively of short talks from leading researchers in the field, designed to maximise scientific exchange and discussion.

The symposium will be organised around two broad themes:
Day 1 - Episodic memory, spatial cognition, and the hippocampus
Day 2 - Speech and language, auditory cognition, and the neocortex

For those interested in only one of these themes, single-day registration options will be available.

We hope that SUSHI will provide a unique opportunity for researchers working with human single-unit recordings to exchange ideas in an intimate setting before joining the broader memory science community at ICOM-7.

Further details, including registration information and the scientific programme, can be found on the symposium website here. You can sign up to receive further updates via the mailing list here.

We would be delighted if you could join us in Glasgow, and grateful if you could share this invitation with any interested parties.

With best wishes,

Daniel Bush & Simon Hanslmayr
On behalf of the SUSHI 2027 Organising Committee

----------------------------------------------------

Dr. Daniel Bush

GM01, Medical Sciences Building, Gower Street, London, WC1E 6BT

Associate Professor, UCL Department of Neuroscience, Physiology and Pharmacology

Principal Investigator, UCL Human Electrophysiology Lab

Co-director, UCL Centre for Neuro-AI

Section Editor, PLoS Computational Biology

topics.title: Postdoctoral Researcher – Developing Cortical Networks at UMN
topics.snippet: Postdoctoral Researcher – In Vivo Imaging and Electrophysiology of Developing Cortical Networks Smith

messages.author: Gordon Smith
messages.title: Postdoctoral Researcher – Developing Cortical Networks at UMN
messages.body_html:
Postdoctoral Researcher – In Vivo Imaging and Electrophysiology of Developing Cortical Networks

Smith Lab – University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN


Before the cortex can process sensory information, its circuits must first organize themselves. The Smith Lab at the University of Minnesota studies how this happens. We have found that distributed, modular networks with millimeter-scale correlations exist throughout the developing neocortex, and using in vivo optogenetics and computational modeling, we have shown that these networks are self-organizing and depend on local intracortical circuitry. We are now asking how early network activity shapes the circuits that emerge: by imaging, recording, and perturbing activity in vivo during development, and comparing the results against models of network self-organization.


The postdoc will lead projects combining two-photon imaging, optogenetics, and electrophysiology in the developing cortex, with the opportunity to shape the direction of their own work.

Recent work: Mulholland, et al. bioRxiv, 2026 ·  Powell, et al. PNAS 2024 · Lab website: smithneurolab.org

For more details, including how to apply please see:

https://www.smithneurolab.org/positions/postdoc-2026

Gordon Smith, Ph. D. 

Associate Professor
Associate Director of Graduate Studies 
Graduate Program of Neuroscience
Optical Imaging and Brain Science Medical Discovery Team
Department of Neuroscience
Center for Magnetic Resonance Research
University of Minnesota

messages.title: Open Rank Faculty Position in Basic Biomedical Research – WashU Medicine
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

The Division of Basic Research in the Department of Anesthesiology at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis is recruiting tenure track or tenured faculty.

Our open rank search welcomes outstanding scientists across all areas of basic biomedical research, including molecular and cellular biology, neuroscience, and related disciplines. We seek creative and innovative investigators who will bring new scientific directions and help shape the future of basic research in our highly collaborative environment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

For additional information and to apply:
https://facultyopportunities.wustl.edu/Posting/Detail/1011265

Please share this opportunity with interested colleagues and trainees.

Thank you!
Wayland Cheng

Dear colleagues,

We are currently recruiting a Postdoctoral Researcher in NHP systems neuroscience to join our team at the Paris Brain Institute (CNRS/Sorbonne Universite), in France. The project uses fMRI-guided neurophysiology to investigate multi-sensory social perception in monkeys and is funded by an ERC Grant (NEURO-SOCIETY).

Link to the position description and application: https://offres.institutducerveau-icm.org/fr/jobs/2021-23  
Enquiries: EMAIL_REDACTED   
Lab website: Neurophysiology of Social Cognition Lab.
Dates: Review of applications will continue until the position is filled

Please don't hesitate to distribute it to potentially interested candidates. 
Many thanks
Julia
